# Darwin Core Term Versions

The Darwin Core terms are versioned in GitHub here:
https://github.com/tdwg/dwc/raw/refs/heads/master/vocabulary/term_versions.csv

Also downloaded BMDE 2.00 to `data/external`.

The [AKN paper](https://research.fs.usda.gov/treesearch/36765) introducing BMDE was published in 2009, though it sounds as though the BMDE standard may have been developed and circulated online around 2005 or 2006. 

The first release of DwC was 2009-10-09, though there are dates earlier than this for terms in the above `term_versions.csv`.

We will first load and take a look at the first rows in the `term_versions.csv`.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(knitr)

TERM_VERSIONS_URL <- "https://github.com/tdwg/dwc/raw/refs/heads/master/vocabulary/term_versions.csv"
BMDE_FIELDS_CSV <- "data/external/bmde_2.00_fields.csv"
DWC_RATIFIED <- as.Date("2009-10-09") # TDWG ratification of the first DwC standard
TODAY <- Sys.Date()
```

```{r}
term_versions_raw <- read.csv(TERM_VERSIONS_URL, na.strings = "", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
head(term_versions_raw)
```
```{r}
nrow(term_versions_raw)
```

So we see that each row gives an iri identifying a version of a given DwC term. Rows have the version's publication date in a separate column, and the status column tells us whether this version of the term has been superseded, recommended (current), or deprecated.

Reformat dates and strip the '#-<int>' version from the iri into a new dataframe

```{r}
term_versions <- term_versions_raw |>
  mutate(
    issued = as.Date(issued, format = "%Y-%m-%d"),
    namespace = str_remove(term_iri, "[^/#]+$")
  )
head(term_versions)
```

Function to get the terms that were in use on a given date.
```{r}
dwc_snapshot <- function(on_date) {
  term_versions |>
    filter(issued <= on_date) |>
    arrange(issued) |>
    group_by(term_iri) |>
    slice_tail(n = 1) |>
    ungroup() |>
    filter(status != "deprecated")
}
```

Now we can get the terms in use in 2009 vs those in use today.
```{r}
dwc_2009 <- dwc_snapshot(DWC_RATIFIED)
dwc_today <- dwc_snapshot(TODAY)
```
